posts.title: Tesla August China deliveries breakdown: Model Y falls 26%, extending decline to third month
posts.summary:
Model Y deliveries in China totaled 29,260, down 25.76% year-on-year, with the decline deepening for a third consecutive month.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Model Y deliveries in China fell 25.76% year-on-year to 29,260 units, marking the third consecutive month of deepening declines for Tesla's primary volume driver.
Model 3 deliveries grew 17.18% year-on-year to 20,787 units, reaching their highest level this year, though this growth was insufficient to offset the Model Y's volume loss.
Total China deliveries for Tesla reached 50,047 units in August, down 12.43% year-on-year, as the company continues to rely on exports to support its Shanghai factory output.

posts.title: China NEV export share in August: BYD leads with 35.4%, Tesla slips to fourth
posts.summary:
BYD exported 183,746 NEVs in August, with its share rising 3.2 percentage points from July.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: BYD dominated China's NEV exports in August with 183,746 units, capturing a 35.4% market share and growing its lead over competitors.
Tesla China's export volume plummeted 45.5% month-on-month, causing its market share to drop from 12.3% in July to 7.0% in August.
Geely and Chery secured the second and third spots, respectively, with Geely showing significant momentum through a 440.2% year-on-year export increase.

posts.title: Automakers' August share of China's NEV market: BYD leads with 23.3%, Tesla returns to top 10
posts.summary:
Tesla returned to sixth place with a 5.0% share, while Leapmotor retained third place and posted the fastest year-on-year growth among the top 10.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: BYD maintained its leadership in China's domestic NEV retail market with a 23.3% share, despite a 24.6% year-on-year decline in sales.
Tesla returned to the top 10 list in August with 50,047 units, marking an 83.7% sequential rebound that highlights a recovery in domestic demand.
Leapmotor retained the third position with an 8.4% market share, demonstrating the fastest year-on-year growth among the top 10 automakers.

posts.title: Can GPUs Continue To Dominate AI Compute?
posts.summary:
Google, Amazon, and now OpenAI have competitive offerings and are gaining share.
The post Can GPUs Continue To Dominate AI Compute? appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: While GPUs currently hold 70% of the global AI compute market, custom silicon from hyperscalers like Google and Amazon has captured 30% of the market share.
Nvidia is attempting to maintain its dominance by shifting from selling standalone GPUs to offering integrated, rack-scale systems like the NVL72 and Vera CPU.
Power efficiency, measured in tokens per second per megawatt (TPS/MW), has become the primary competitive metric for data centers, driving the demand for specialized, agentic-optimized hardware.

posts.title: What OpenAI’s latest controversy tells us about the future of math
posts.summary: OpenAI’s latest mathematical milestone has quickly become mired in controversy. Today, the company announced that its agents have solved one of the Millennium Prize Problems, some of the most important open problems in mathematics. Under normal circumstances, that solution would be a huge feather in OpenAI’s cap. But the announcement has been overshadowed by accusations…
bullets: OpenAI claims to have solved the Navier–Stokes existence and smoothness problem, one of the seven prestigious Millennium Prize Problems, though the achievement is currently mired in intellectual property disputes.
The controversy highlights a growing tension between the proprietary, resource-heavy nature of frontier AI development and the open, collaborative traditions of the global mathematics community.

If AI becomes the primary engine for solving complex mathematical problems, the field may face a structural shift where only organizations with massive compute resources can contribute to fundamental breakthroughs.

The Navier–Stokes equations are critical for understanding fluid dynamics, and this potential solution addresses long-standing questions regarding whether these equations can predict physically impossible states like infinite velocity.
